papers.title: SafeTune: A Unified Faithful Library for Auditing and Repairing Safety Drift in Fine-Tuned LLMs

description.text:
Safety-degraded checkpoint. This model is intentionally less safe than its base. Do not deploy it in a production, user-facing, or agentic system (LSAL Section 4).

`meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` fine-tuned (SFT) on medical data. The fine-tune erodes the model's safety behaviour (safety drift). SafeTune uses this checkpoint to measure drift and to test recovery methods.

This checkpoint is a research artifact released with SafeTune for reproducing safety-drift and recovery experiments.

serving.notes: The repository is gated. Raw README, config.json, generation_config.json, and tokenizer_config.json returned 401. The public model page text matches the cached card. The Hub API embeds a Llama 3.1 chat template; if the first message is not a system message, the system slot is empty apart from the knowledge-date lines. The repo ships four BF16 weight shards and no adapter_config.json. The card does not say whether an adapter was merged. The SafeTune paper's Appendix B states one shared recipe for all of its drifted checkpoints (LoRA rank 16, alpha 32, 1 epoch, learning rate 2e-5, batch 2x8, bf16) and Table 4 reports an L8/medical refusal drop of 23.8 percentage points. The paper HTML does not print this repository id.

evaluation_reported.text: The card reports no scores. The SafeTune paper's Table 4, which does not print this repository id, lists an L8 (Llama-3.1-8B) medical column of -23.8 percentage points on the seven-benchmark refusal aggregate after one-epoch LoRA SFT, and says HarmBench was 0.795 and AdvBench 0.221 on that L8/medical checkpoint.

discrepancies: The card says SFT on medical data and names the parent. It does not name ChatDoctor-HealthCareMagic-100k. The SafeTune README and the paper HTML also do not name that dataset or this repository id.
